newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end stronger on fund demand.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end stronger on fund demand.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed higher as late fund buying offset scattered selling interest, traders said.

Live cattle futures were slipping from highs late following the posting of lower beef prices again at midday. But futures held above previous levels going into the close which prompted funds to add to long positions, traders said.
Futures had traded on both sides of previous levels early. Short covering developed following reports of active feedlot sales late Thursday which offset weakness in beef, they said.
"The futures market may be near to bottoming," one trader said noting the lack of selling interest after the initial setback in prices.

Feedlots generally are keeping current in their marketings in the southern and central Plains and cattle feeders were seen asking $67 to $68 for cattle next week, especially with packers apparently short of supplies. Live weights are down and cattle could use more days on feed, traders added.

USDA estimated the average weight of cattle slaughtered under federal inspection the week ended January 4 at 1,163 lbs, down from 1,166 lbs estimated the previous week and well below the year-ago actual weight of 1,209 lbs.

Cargill Investor Services, LFG, E.D.&F. Man and Refco bought February late while R.J. O'Brien purchased April to offset selling by local options traders, floor sources said. RBH and Rosenthal Collins bought February early while Prudential Securities bought February and April. E.D.&F. Man spread long February/short June early, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, volatility was weak on mixed selling of February 62 to 66 puts. Commission houses sold April 62 puts, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle futures followed the lead of live cattle with lower corn futures reinforcing gains, traders said.

LFG turned a seller in January and March late but buying by Refco in March and scattered demand in January kept futures supported. Cargill spread long October 1997 feeders/short February 1998 live cattle early and spsread long August live cattle/short March feeders late. Lond-Waldock spread long June live cattle/short January feeders, pit sources said.
Live cattle closed 0.250 cent a lb higher to 0.025 lower with February up 0.225 at 65.025 cents per lb. Feeder cattle finished up 0.325 to 0.175 cent with March up 0.225 at 67.900 cents.
